title: Adaptive Access Engine: what it is, prerequisites, profiles, signal history and overrides

prose.label: Where signals come from.
prose.text: The vendor integrations (Okta, CrowdStrike, Microsoft Defender and Silverfort), their setup and the signals each sends are in [[unified.adaptive-access.integrations]]. Which signals UEBA and Zscaler risk scores carry is not stated {{gap:risk-score-signals}}.

prose.label: Profiles.
prose.text: {{profile-definition}} {{profiles-page}} {{add-prerequisites}} {{criteria}} {{evaluation}} {{enforcement}} {{delete-confirmation}} The policy criteria that consume a profile are in [[zpa.policy.criteria]], [[zia.url-filtering.criteria]] and [[zia.cloud-app-control.rule-criteria]]. What subscribing to Experience Center changes for the criterion is open {{gap:subscription-licensing}}.

prose.label: Signal History.
prose.text: {{signal-history}} {{signal-history-value}} Whether the Value column can show the finer levels a source sends, such as the Defender levels in [[unified.adaptive-access.integrations:defender-signals]], is open {{gap:signal-history-value-levels}}; retention, time ranges, export and the Context Type values are not stated {{gap:signal-history-retention}}.

prose.label: Overrides.
prose.text: {{overrides}} {{override-controls}} {{overrides-page}} The expiry limits and where the audit logging lands are not stated {{gap:override-expiry-audit}}.

prose.label: Timing and APIs.
prose.text: The latency from a signal to enforcement is described only as real time {{gap:signal-latency}}. The SDK, Terraform and legacy API surfaces for profiles have not been read {{gap:profile-api-unmined}}.

checks.do: That the integrations for the third-party tools the profile uses were completed before the profile was defined.
That Authentication Service for end users, the Zscaler Admin Console and Internet & SaaS or Private Access are in use before expecting the engine to evaluate signals.
For a user or device whose signal value looks wrong, the Signal History row for its subject and the Overrides page for a time-bound override that replaces the source value.
For a Signal History Value, which source sent it, since the Value column's levels are given as (Low, High) while a source can send finer levels.

what-it-is.statement: The Adaptive Access Engine ingests security signals and distributes adaptive access profiles in real time to policy decision points, so security policies can be evaluated and adapted by the nature of the identities, their profiles and the applications being accessed; adaptive access control is enforced at policy enforcement points in Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Private Access (ZPA), and the events analyzed might occur inside or outside the Zscaler ecosystem.

quotes: Zscaler offers continuous adaptive access to monitor users, devices, and security context to enforce adaptive access control at policy enforcement points in Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Private Access (ZPA).

The Zscaler Adaptive Access Engine ingests security signals and distributes adaptive access profiles in real time to policy decision points, so security policies can be evaluated and adapted based on the nature of the identities, their profiles, and the applications being accessed.
The Adaptive Access Engine provides a unified way to analyze and interpret events in a specific context to derive insightful results.
These events might occur inside or outside the Zscaler ecosystem.

signal-sources.statement: The vendor lists as benefits using real-time signals from Zscaler and third-party security systems to adjust user access, and integrating user risk profiles, device postures and behavioral analytics into access decisions.

quotes: Real-Time Risk Mitigation: Leverage real-time signals from Zscaler and third-party security systems, to dynamically adjust user access
Enhanced Security Posture: Integrate diverse signals (user risk profiles, device postures, behavioral analytics) into access decisions

prerequisites.statement: To use the Adaptive Access Engine an organization must have Authentication Service for end users enabled (or end user migration to it completed), the Zscaler Admin Console enabled, and Internet & SaaS or Private Access in use; for an organization that does not meet these, Zscaler recommends migrating its admins and its end users to Authentication Service.

quotes: To leverage Adaptive Access Engine, your organization must meet the following prerequisites:
Authentication Service for end users is enabled or end user migration to Authentication Service is completed.
Zscaler Admin Console is enabled.
Internet & SaaS or Private Access is used.
If your organization does not meet these prerequisites, Zscaler recommends that you complete the following steps to be able to use Adaptive Access Engine:
Migrate your admins to Authentication Service.
Migrate your end users to Authentication Service.

profile-definition.statement: An Adaptive Access profile identifies user and device subjects with a set of conditions that combine context signals published by Zscaler and third-party sources using logical operators; profiles are made available to Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Private Applications (ZPA), which enforce policies to control user and device access to applications.

quotes: An Adaptive Access profile identifies user and device subjects with a set of conditions that combine context signals published by Zscaler and third-party sources using logical operators.

The Adaptive Access profiles are made available to Internet & SaaS (Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA)) and Private Applications (Zscaler Private Access (ZPA)) that enforce policies to control user and device access to applications via Zscaler.

profiles-page.statement: The Profiles page (Policies > Common Configuration > Adaptive Access > Profiles) lists each profile with a Profile Name (unique), Description, Last Modified On and Criteria (context signals combined with logical operators), and profiles can be added, searched, edited, deleted and copied there.

quotes: On the Profiles page (Policies > Common Configuration > Adaptive Access > Profiles)
Profile Name: A unique name for the profile.
Description: The description for the profile.
Last Modified On: The date and time the profile was last updated.
Criteria: The criteria that are defined by combining the context signals using logical operators.
Copy the profile.
Add a profile.
Search for the required profile.
Edit the profile.
Delete the profile.

add-prerequisites.statement: The integrations with the third-party services relevant to the organization (such as Okta, CrowdStrike, Microsoft Defender or Silverfort) must be completed before profiles are defined, and only administrators can add profiles.

quotes: You must complete the integration of third-party services, such as Okta, CrowdStrike, Microsoft Defender, or Silverfort that are relevant to your organization, before defining the Adaptive Access profiles.
Only administrators can add the Adaptive Access profiles.

criteria.statement: A profile takes a Profile Name, an optional Description and Criteria joined by All or Any; each criterion selects the third-party tool the context signal comes from, the event to monitor (the events differ for each tool) and an operator, logical expression, condition or numerical value, and a JSON expression is updated automatically as the criteria are defined.

quotes: Profile Name: Provide a name for the profile.
(Optional) Description: Enter a short description, if required.
Criteria: Select All or Any from the drop-down menu, then click the Add icon to define the criteria.
Select the third-party tool from where the context signal must be received.
Select the event that must be monitored. The events or incidents differ for each third-party tool.
Select the Operator, logical expression, condition, or numerical value, as required.
The JSON expression is automatically updated as you define the criteria.

enforcement.statement: Any user or device matching a profile's criteria is notified to the policy enforcement points, Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Private Applications (ZPA); the page says UEBA and Zscaler risk scores can be added via the Adaptive Access Engine and attached to Internet & SaaS and Private Access policies.

quotes: Any user or device that matches the profile criteria is notified to the policy enforcement points (Internet & SaaS (Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA)) and Private Applications (Zscaler Private Access (ZPA)))
You can add User Entity and Behavior Analytics (UEBA) and Zscaler risk scores via the Adaptive Access Engine and attach them to the Internet & SaaS and Private Access policies.

evaluation.statement: The engine evaluates the context signals it receives against the profile criteria, and the signals are displayed on the Signal History page.

quotes: The Adaptive Access Engine receives context signals which are evaluated against the profile criteria, and these signals are displayed on the Signal History page.

delete-confirmation.statement: Deleting a profile requires entering YES in the Confirmation window and clicking Delete; edits are made in the Edit Profiles window and saved with Update.

quotes: In the Confirmation window, enter YES, then click Delete.
In the Edit Profiles window, modify the values as required.
Click Update.

signal-history.statement: The Signal History page (Policies > Common Configuration > Adaptive Access > Signal History) shows the context signals for each Adaptive Access profile; each signal has a Subject (the username or device type), Subject Type (the user or device activity that triggered the event), Source (the page gives Okta, CrowdStrike, Microsoft Defender as the sources), Context Type (the type of signal received) and Creation (when the signal was generated), and the table can be filtered, searched, reset and its columns modified.

quotes: You can view and analyze the context signals for each Adaptive Access profile.
On the Signal History page (Policies > Common Configuration > Adaptive Access > Signal History)
Subject: The username or device type for which the signal is logged.
Subject Type: The user or device activity that triggered this event.
Source: The source (Okta, CrowdStrike, Microsoft Defender) from where the context signal was received.
Context Type: The type of signal received.
Creation: The date and time the signal was generated.
Use the filters to view specific information.
Reset the page to the original settings.
Search for a specific context signal.
Modify the table and its columns.

signal-history-value.statement: The Signal History page describes the Value column as the risk (Low, High) associated with the user or device.

quotes: Value: The risk (Low, High) associated with the user or device.

overrides.statement: Overrides are time-bound changes set by admins to a subject's (user or device) context signal value that temporarily replace the signal value from the context source, such as Okta or CrowdStrike, while retaining the original value for reference and auditing; they take effect immediately across the Adaptive Access Engine-driven evaluations (for example Internet & SaaS or Private Access), so the next access attempt reflects the change.

quotes: Overrides are time-bound changes set by admins to a subject’s (user or device) context signal value that temporarily replace the signal value from the context source, such as Okta, CrowdStrike, etc., while retaining the original value for reference and auditing.
Overrides take effect immediately across the Adaptive Access Engine-driven evaluations (e.g., Internet & SaaS or Private Access), so the next access attempt reflects the change.

override-controls.statement: Overrides rectify inaccurate signal values from the context source or make urgent exceptions; they carry mandatory expiration and audit logging, and only context signals can be overridden, not profiles directly.

quotes: Overrides are required to rectify inaccurate signal values from the context source or make urgent exceptions
Overrides help maintain control and accountability via mandatory expiration and audit logging.
They preserve policy integrity by only allowing context-signal overrides and not direct profile overrides.

overrides-page.statement: The Overrides page (Policies > Common Configuration > Adaptive Access > Overrides) shows each Subject Identifier (the login ID of the user or device), Subject Type (user or device), Context Count (context signals received) and Override Count (the number of overrides).

quotes: Go to Policies > Common Configuration > Adaptive Access > Overrides.
Subject Identifier: The login ID of the user or device.
Subject Type: The type of subject (user or device).
Context Count: The number of context signals received.
Override Count: The number of overrides.

signal-history-value-levels.title: Whether the Signal History Value column can show the finer levels a source sends
signal-history-value-levels.detail: The Signal History page gives the Value as 'the risk (Low, High)'; the Microsoft Defender page lists Risk Score values None, Informational, Low, Medium and High and Exposure Level values None, Low, Medium and High (unified.adaptive-access.integrations:defender-signals). The Signal History parenthetical may be illustrative. No page says that the Value column and a Defender signal value are the same field, so this is recorded as scoped claims and not as a divergence.

signal-history-retention.title: Signal History retention, time ranges, export and Context Type values
signal-history-retention.detail: The Signal History page's benefit list says admins can view the list of context signals for specific durations; it gives no retention period, range values or export, and does not list the Context Type values. Its Source example omits Silverfort.

override-expiry-audit.title: Override expiry limits and where override audit logging lands
override-expiry-audit.detail: Expiration is called mandatory, but no default or maximum duration is given, and the audit log that records overrides is not named: the Experience Center audit log category list has no Adaptive Access entry.

signal-latency.title: Latency from a signal to enforcement
signal-latency.detail: The pages describe distribution as real time, and overrides as immediate; no figure is given.

risk-score-signals.title: Which signals and values UEBA and Zscaler risk scores carry through the engine
risk-score-signals.detail: One sentence says UEBA and Zscaler risk scores can be added via the Adaptive Access Engine; which signals and values they carry is not stated. The page points to Understanding Risk Score, which is not captured in this area.

subscription-licensing.title: What subscribing to Experience Center changes for the Adaptive Access criterion
subscription-licensing.detail: The prerequisites list Authentication Service, the Zscaler Admin Console and Internet & SaaS or Private Access. This narrows but does not close the zia.cloud-app-control.rule-criteria gap adaptive-access-experience-center.

profile-api-unmined.title: API, SDK and Terraform surfaces for Adaptive Access profiles
profile-api-unmined.detail: Not mined: the ZIA Go SDK zscaler/zia/services/adaptive_access/adaptive_access.go (endpoint /zia/api/v1/adaptiveAccessProfiles, handler /profiles/rules), the ZIA Terraform data source zia_adaptive_access_profile (name, iam_aap_ids and org_id lookups) and the Python SDK zscaler/zia/legacy.py. The ZIA OpenAPI /riskProfiles paths are a different object. The ZPA operand side is in zpa.policy.criteria.
